newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac confirms fully franked dividends.
newsitem.headline: Westpac confirms fully franked dividends.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Tuesday it would maintain its policy of paying fully franked dividends for the foreseeable future.

Westpac said it was making the statement in response to an article in the Australian Financial Review which suggested a crackdown on dividend washing would restrain its capacity to fully frank dividends.
"Westpac has not and does not intend to rely on so-called "dividend washing or arbitrage" to pay fully franked dividends," the company said in a statement.
Westpac said it had stated on May 14 that it intended to maintain fully franked dividends for the foreseeable future and nothing had arisen to alter this statement.

Dividend washing is a practice where Australian investors temporarily buy stock from foreigners who cannot use franking credits. These offer provide a tax rebate based on the amount of tax paid by a company.
Westpac paid a dividend of 19 cents per share for the six months to March 31, 1997 and a total dividend of 33 cents per share for the year to September 30, 1996.
